sections.content:
The board looks the same - still the diagonal split. The SPACE didn't change the lower block because the upper block is purple and the lower block already has purple on top (diagonal). So SPACE with same color = no change.
Let me step back and think about what I know:
1. The template is white/purple (horizontal split)
2. I can create:
   - [p, W] (purple top, white bottom) - horizontal split
   - [W] (all white) - merged
   - Diagonal split (purple top-right, white bottom-left) - when upper is diamond
3. I need [W, p] (white top, purple bottom) - horizontal split
I haven't tried using the diamond to create a diagonal split with white on top-right and purple on bottom-left. Let me try:
- Set upper to white
- Rotate to diamond (RIGHT)
- SPACE to create diagonal split with white on top-right
Then from there, maybe I can convert the diagonal to horizontal somehow.
Actually, wait. Let me reconsider the problem. Maybe the goal isn't to match the template exactly. Maybe the goal is something else entirely.
Let me look at the template and the current lower block:
- Template: white top, purple bottom (horizontal)
- Lower block: diagonal split (purple top-right, white bottom-left)
What if the goal is to make the lower block match the template? Then I need white on top, purple on bottom.
But I can only create:
- Horizontal split with upper color on top
- Diagonal split with upper color on top-right
- Merged block with upper color
So to get white on top, I need upper=white and square shape, then SPACE. But that gives me all white (merged), not a split.
Wait, no. Let me re-examine my earlier experiments:
- Lower block [p, W], upper=white → merge to [W] (because upper color != top half color, so it should split... but it merged instead)
Hmm, actually let me re-examine. The rule might be:
- If upper color == ANY part of the lower block: merge to upper color
- If upper color != ANY part of the lower block: split with upper color on top
So:
- Lower [p, W], upper=purple → purple is in lower → merge? No, it stayed [p, W]
- Lower [p, W], upper=white → white is in lower → merge to white? Yes, it became [W]
- Lower [W], upper=purple → purple not in lower → split to [p, W]? Yes!
- Lower [W], upper=white → white is in lower → merge? No change (already all white)
Wait, that doesn't work either. Let me re-examine:
- Lower [p, W], upper=purple → no change (stayed [p, W])
- Lower [p, W], upper=white → merged to [W]
- Lower [W], upper=purple → split to [p, W]
- Lower [W], upper=white → no change (stayed [W])
Pattern:
- If lower is split and upper == top half color: no change
- If lower is split and upper != top half color: merge to upper color
- If lower is merged and upper != lower color: split with upper on top
- If lower is merged and upper == lower color: no change
So SPACE toggles between split and merged:
- Split → if upper == top: stay split; if upper != top: merge to upper
- Merged → if upper == block: stay merged; if upper != block: split with upper on top
This means I can only create splits with the upper color on top. To get white on top, I'd need upper=white and a merged lower block, but upper=white == lower=white, so no split.
UNLESS I use the diagonal split somehow. What if I:
1. Create diagonal split (upper=purple, diamond)
2. Then somehow convert diagonal to horizontal
Or what if I need to use the cursor position? Earlier I thought the cursor didn't matter, but maybe it does in some way I haven't discovered.
Let me try a different approach. What if I:
1. Reset lower to all white (upper=white, SPACE)
2. Set upper to purple
3. RIGHT to diamond
4. SPACE to create diagonal split
5. Then LEFT to un-rotate to square
6. SPACE again to see if it converts diagonal to horizontal
Actually wait, I should first check what the current state is. Let me check if the lower block is still diagonal.

action(['LEFT'])
